title: Grilled Corn Pancakes with Chilli and Herbs
changes_from_base: A savoury batter of cornmeal and a little flour bound with half the corn puréed with chilli, coriander, basil, garlic, lime juice and egg; the rest of the kernels stay whole and the pancakes are shallow-fried, with no buttermilk or sugar.
summary: Golden, herb-flecked pancakes built from leftover grilled corn, lifted with fresh chilli, lime and herbs for a vibrant savoury brunch or side.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
corn kernels (leftover grilled corn is best)
fresh chilli (jalapeño, Thai, serrano or habanero), minced, or to taste
neutral oil (grapeseed or corn), about 6 mm deep in the pan
lime, in wedges, and minced chilli, to serve (optional)

steps.title: Mix
steps.text: Mix the 70 g cornmeal, 65 g plain flour, salt and pepper in a large bowl.

steps.title: Purée
steps.text: Put half of the 600 g corn kernels in a food processor with the minced chilli, 10 g coriander, 10 g basil, 1 tsp minced garlic, the lime juice and 1 egg, and roughly purée, leaving some texture.

steps.title: Combine
steps.text: Stir the purée and the remaining corn into the dry mix.

steps.title: Fry
steps.text: Heat about 6 mm oil in a large frying pan and spoon in large pancakes, turning carefully once.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot, with lime wedges and extra minced chilli if you like.

tips: Use leftover grilled corn if you have it, as it gives the best flavour.
Purée only half the corn so the pancakes keep some bite from whole kernels.
Keep the oil at a steady heat so the pancakes turn golden without burning before the centre cooks through.
storage: These are best eaten fresh and warm, straight from the pan. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
